title: World Cup Fans Can't Get Enough of America's Giant Food and Yellow School Buses
summary: Have you ever traveled to another country and found something totally ordinary that blew your mind? That's happening right now for thousands of soccer fans visiting the U.S. for the World Cup. They're discovering everyday American things—and going wild for them. Rinta Goto, a 24-year-old from Japan, can't stop thinking about the bread at Texas Roadhouse in Dallas. He called it "insanely good" and the steak "ridiculously delicious." His post about it got over 200,000 views! When he found out the restaurant has locations in other countries but not Japan, he put his head in his hands and asked, "Why isn't Japan on the list?" He also loved the free soda refills at McDonald's and the huge bag of Reese's candy at Walmart. Goto isn't the only one. Fans are posting about giant portion sizes, yellow school buses, Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders, and even Buc-ee's, the mega gas station. Some are so excited they plan to come back just for the food and people. One English fan said he was "wowed" by Kansas City and its barbecue. But not everyone believes the posts are real. Some people wonder if they're fake. Still, experts say this is good for America's image around the world, especially when many countries are upset with U.S. leaders. For now, the World Cup is making a lot of visitors say something surprising: "I'm excited to go back to Dallas."
why_it_matters: This shows that what seems normal to you might be amazing to someone from another country, and sharing your culture can help people understand each other better.

background_read: The FIFA World Cup is the biggest soccer tournament in the world, taking place every four years.
In 2026, the United States is hosting the World Cup along with Canada and Mexico, bringing millions of international visitors.
When people travel to a new country, they often notice everyday things that locals find normal but visitors find exciting and different.
Article_Structure: WHO: Rinta Goto, a 24-year-old from Japan, and other international soccer fans visiting the U.S. for the World Cup.

WHAT: They are discovering and posting online about ordinary American things — like Texas Roadhouse bread, free soda refills, giant portions, yellow school buses, and Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders — and reacting with amazement.
WHERE: In Dallas, Texas (at Texas Roadhouse, McDonald's, Walmart, Buc-ee's) and Kansas City (for its barbecue).
WHY: Because these everyday items are totally different from what they have at home, and experts say these genuine reactions can actually help America's image around the world.

perspectives.description: American restaurants and stores are getting lots of happy visitors, and the excitement could make more tourists want to come back.
Some people question if the social media posts are real or if they were made up to get attention.
Experts say that even simple, genuine stories from visitors can improve how people around the world see the United States, especially during times of political tension.
